claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has favorable plasticity and machinability but relatively low hardness and strength.
The starting CoCrFeNiTi alloy is in a simple solid-solution state.
High configurational entropy suppresses ordered intermetallic phase formation in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
Suppression of ordered intermetallic phases maintains a simple solid-solution microstructure.
The simple solid-solution microstructure reduces dislocation pinning.
Reduced dislocation pinning limits strain-hardening capacity.
Reduced dislocation pinning and limited strain hardening lead to lower hardness and strength.
Reduced dislocation pinning and limited strain hardening improve plasticity and machinability.
Increasing Ti or Co beyond the equimolar ratio reduces the alloy's configurational entropy.
Reducing configurational entropy by changing Ti or Co concentration promotes ordered intermetallic phases or precipitates.
Formation of ordered intermetallic phases increases hardness and compressive strength relative to equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
Formation of ordered intermetallic phases decreases plasticity and machinability relative to equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The proposed comparison is limited to room-temperature uniaxial compression up to 500 MPa.
The hypothesis is limited to compositionally varied CoCrFeNiTi alloys and excludes different base-element systems and processing methods.
